editorial:
Imagine moving your whole family into a new place in Madrid during the 1970s, only to find out the apartment has a dark secret. You follow the Olmedo family as they try to start over, but the house they picked is definitely not empty. It starts with small, creepy things, but quickly turns into a nightmare as a ghostly presence begins to mess with their heads. The vibe is heavy and tense, making you feel like something is always watching you from the corners of the room. It blends the scary stuff with the real-life political stress of Spain at that time, which adds a cool layer to the story.

The acting is solid, and the way the scares build up keeps you on edge. While the middle part slows down a bit, the payoff is worth it. If you like ghost stories that focus on family secrets, you will love this one.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a shock when you learn the ghost is actually a former tenant who was murdered. The spirits try to warn the family about the evil in the walls. In the final rush, the family has to fight off the supernatural force to survive. It wraps up with the truth coming out about the apartment's history, leaving you with a feeling that some places are just too cursed to live in.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves haunted house stories and family dramas.
